Rebuilding of the Temple
ree-BIL-ding uhv thuh TEM-puhl
noun
From rebuild + temple; the restoration of the temple after the Babylonian exile, under Zerubbabel and Joshua.

Biblical Definition

The rebuilding of the temple is the restoration of the house of the LORD at Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, when Cyrus king of Persia, stirred up by the LORD, proclaimed that the people might return and build. Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest led the returning remnant, set up the altar, and laid the foundation, at which the old men who had seen the first house wept aloud while the young men shouted for joy. The work was hindered by the adversaries of Judah and ceased for years, until the LORD raised up the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, who stirred the people to build, rebuking their care for their own panelled houses while the house of God lay waste. By the word of the LORD the work went forward and was finished, and the house was dedicated with joy. Though this second temple lacked the glory of Solomon’s—the ark, the visible glory—the LORD promised by Haggai that the glory of this latter house should be greater than the former, and that He would fill it with glory—a word fulfilled when the Lord Christ Himself, the Desire of all nations, entered its courts. The dictionary honors the rebuilding of the temple as a testimony to the faithfulness of God to His covenant and His word, to the duty of putting His house and worship before our own ease, and to the surpassing glory that came not in gold but in the presence of the incarnate Son.

Webster 1828 Definition

The restoration of the temple after the exile under Zerubbabel and Joshua; hindered, then finished by the word of the LORD through Haggai and Zechariah.

REBUILDING OF THE TEMPLE, the restoration of the LORD’s house after exile.

Cyrus proclaimed the return; Zerubbabel and Joshua led the remnant.

The foundation was laid; the old wept, the young shouted for joy.

Hindered for years, then stirred by Haggai and Zechariah.

Its latter glory greater, fulfilled when Christ entered its courts.

Key Scripture

Ezr 1:3 — "Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem."

Hag 1:4 — "Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?"

Hag 2:9 — "The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts."

Ezr 6:14 — "And the elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia."

Modern Corruption

The rebuilding is read as mere national restoration; Scripture frames it as covenant faithfulness, the duty of God’s house before our ease, and the promise fulfilled in Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the merely political reading that treats the rebuilding as a national restoration project under Persian patronage, missing its covenantal and prophetic weight. Scripture sees the hand of God throughout: the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus to proclaim the return (Ezr 1:3), and the work prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah and was finished according to the commandment of the God of Israel (Ezr 6:14). The empire was the instrument; the LORD was the builder.

The principle to recover is threefold. First, the faithfulness of God to His covenant and His word: He brought His people back and restored His worship as He had promised. Second, the duty of putting God’s house before our own ease—Haggai rebuked the people for dwelling in their panelled houses while the house of God lay waste (Hag 1:4), and the rebuke still searches a church that lavishes care on its own comfort while the worship of God languishes. Third, the surpassing glory that came not in gold: the LORD promised the latter house a greater glory (Hag 2:9), fulfilled not in splendour of building but in the entrance of the incarnate Son, the Desire of all nations, into its courts.

Hebrew Roots

Rebuild + temple; the restoration of the LORD’s house after exile under Zerubbabel and Joshua, finished by His word and crowned by Christ’s coming.
